title: Sal's walk-in freezer died in the heat. 'Forty pounds of pastrami, my friend. Forty.'

options.label: Haul it to your fridge
options.cost: 15 Energy and every shelf you own
options.riskWhy: Pastrami is heavy, Sal is grateful

outcomes.text: Six trips up your stairs with pastrami in your arms. Your fridge is now a deli. Sal says nothing, then says 'good,' which from Sal is a parade.

later.text: Remember the pastrami relay? Sal put a sandwich on the board with your name on it. It sells. He hands you C$120 in 'royalties' and denies it.

options.label: Sell it to the carts on the side

outcomes.text: You move forty pounds of 'spoiled' pastrami to three carts on Steinway by sundown. C$300, and Sal thinks it went in the dumpster.
Three carts, C$300, no questions. Sal waves at you the next morning like nothing happened. Which is how Sal waves when something happened.

later.text: Remember Sal's 'spoiled' pastrami? A cart on Steinway had it on special. Sal recognized his own slicing from across the street. You paid him back. All of it.
later.headline: Developing: {name} sold a bodega's rescued pastrami to street carts. Sal: 'Twenty-two years on this corner. I know my own slice.' 👀

options.label: Not today
options.riskWhy: Nobody keeps score of a no

outcomes.text: You wish Sal luck. He nods and starts making a sandwich the size of a toddler, alone. Respect.

title: Sal's cat has been gone two days. 'Not my cat. The store's cat. Find her, please.'

options.label: Search the whole block
options.get: A cat back on the bread
options.riskWhy: Cats come home when they feel like it

outcomes.text: You find her asleep in the laundromat's lost-and-found, on someone's good sweater. Sal pretends not to be relieved for almost four seconds.
Two hours of 'pspsps' up and down 31st Street. She strolls back on her own at midnight. Sal still gives you the credit, and a free roll.

options.label: Find her, charge a finder's fee
options.riskWhy: Sal knows where the cat goes

outcomes.text: You bring her back and say 'C$150, standard rate.' Sal pays from the register very slowly, one bill at a time, looking at you the whole way.

later.text: Remember the cat finder's fee? Turns out she visits the laundromat every Thursday. Sal knew. He told the whole stoop you charged him for a Thursday.

options.label: Not today
options.riskWhy: Nobody keeps score of a no

outcomes.text: You tell Sal she'll turn up. He says 'everyone says that' and goes back to staring at the door.

title: Sal's landlord wants 40% more. 'Mira, you're good with phones. Help me write back?'

options.label: Write the letter with him
options.cost: 10 Energy and a night of polite fury
options.riskWhy: Landlords come and go. Mostly come.

outcomes.text: Two drafts, one backgammon break and a final letter so polite it's terrifying. Sal signs it like a treaty.

later.text: Remember the letter to Sal's landlord? He folded to 8%. Sal hands you an envelope marked NOT A TIP. It's C$200. It's a tip.

outcomes.text: The landlord doesn't budge an inch. Sal pays it, tears the letter into confetti, and gives you a coffee for trying.

options.label: Tip off a realtor about the lease
options.riskWhy: Fran answers every phone on 31st Street

outcomes.text: You mention the lease to No-Fee* Realty and a C$400 'lead fee' lands the same day. Somewhere, a luxury condo sign gets printed.

later.text: Remember the tip to No-Fee* Realty? Fran told Sal who called. Sal stopped saying good morning to you. The whole block noticed before you did.
later.headline: BREAKING: Sources say {name} sold out Sal's lease to a realtor for a 'lead fee.' The cat has been told. 👀

title: Jojo's film school interview is in an hour. 'Cover the bar? It's just coffee. And rumors.'

options.label: Cover her shift
options.cost: 18 Energy and three hours of oat milk
options.riskWhy: Laptop campers can smell a new barista

outcomes.text: You spell every name wrong on purpose and nobody notices. Jojo runs back in shrieking. The interview went 'deadass perfect.'

later.text: Remember covering Jojo's shift? She got in. Her first short film thanks you in the credits. Your name is spelled wrong. On purpose.

options.label: Cover it, skim the tip jar
options.cost: Jojo's film school, one tip at a time
options.riskWhy: Jojo counts that jar to the quarter

outcomes.text: Three hours, one shift, C$180 lighter jar. You tell Jojo it was 'a slow day.' It was not a slow day. It's never a slow day.

later.text: Remember the light tip jar? Jojo counts it every night. For a week she wrote 'THIEF' on your cup, spelled right for once. You paid it back.

options.label: Can't, sorry
options.riskWhy: Nobody keeps score of a no

outcomes.text: You can't today. Jojo calls her cousin, who arrives in pajamas and makes everyone a cortado nobody ordered.

title: Grind & Gossip's espresso machine is screaming. 'Deadass, it's possessed. You know machines?'

options.label: Fix it with a butter knife
options.get: A working machine and a hero's latte
options.cost: 10 Energy and a steam burn's worth of nerves

outcomes.text: One butter knife, one YouTube tutorial on mute, one loud hiss. It works. The café applauds. Jojo names a drink 'The Exorcist.'
It works, mostly. It now sings a little while it steams. Jojo says it's better this way and tips you in gossip.

options.label: Call it dead, buy it, flip it

outcomes.text: You tell Jojo it's a goner and take it off her hands for C$50 'to be nice.' A screwdriver and a listing later, it's worth C$400.

later.text: Remember the 'dead' espresso machine? It's on a resale listing, and your face is in the chrome. Jojo screenshotted it before you could blink. You refunded half.
later.headline: Developing: {name} called a café's espresso machine 'dead,' then sold it working. Jojo: 'I heard it before it happened.' 👀

title: A laptop camper has had Jojo's best table nine hours on one water. 'Get him out, nicely?'

options.label: Charm him out the door
options.cost: 8 Energy and some of your best small talk

outcomes.text: You ask about his startup. Forty minutes later he leaves to 'take a call with himself.' Jojo slides you a large with extra rumor.

options.label: Rent him the table by the hour
options.cost: Jojo's café, sold out from under her

outcomes.text: You tell him the table is 'premium seating now, C$40 an hour.' He pays. He stays. Jojo watches you pocket it from behind the register.

later.text: Remember charging rent at Grind & Gossip? The camper left a review: 'Great tables, strict landlord.' Jojo printed it and taped it to the door, with your name.

options.label: Not today
options.riskWhy: Nobody keeps score of a no

outcomes.text: You tell Jojo you're not built for confrontation. She sighs and turns the Wi-Fi off. He leaves in four minutes.

title: Mags's barback quit mid-shift. 'Two hundred thirsty people and me. Grab the ice?'

options.label: Haul ice all night
options.riskWhy: Ice is heavy and the stairs are dark

outcomes.text: Forty bags of ice, three spilled trays, one standing ovation from the bar. Mags slides you water like it's champagne.

later.text: Remember hauling ice for Mags? You're on Velvet Static's list now, plus one, for good. Brock Squarejaw asked the door who you were.

options.label: Pour free shots for your followers

outcomes.text: Behind the bar for one hour and every follower you have drinks free. The stories go everywhere. Mags is too busy to notice. Tonight.

later.text: Remember those free shots at Velvet Static? Mags counted the bottles. You paid for every one, and the doorman has your photo now.

options.label: Not today
options.riskWhy: Nobody keeps score of a no

outcomes.text: You say you're off the clock. Mags says 'same,' and keeps pouring with two hands.

title: Brock Squarejaw tipped Mags in autographs again. 'Help me sell these so I can make rent?'

options.label: Sell them for her, fair price
options.cost: 8 Energy and an afternoon of collectors

outcomes.text: You find three collectors and one very emotional fan. Mags makes rent. She says it's the first time Brock has been useful.

later.text: Remember selling Brock's autographs for Mags? She insisted on a cut. C$100, slid across the bar under a coaster.

outcomes.text: Mags's stack sells, and so do the twelve you signed at home. C$300 extra. Your Brock has a nice loop on the B.

later.text: Remember the extra Brock Squarejaw autographs? Half of them say 'Brok.' His team called Mags. Mags called you, very loudly. You bought them all back.
later.headline: BREAKING: Fake Brock Squarejaw autographs flood Astoria. Sources trace them to {name}. Brock: 'I would never write a B like that.'

title: Chardonnay Shade left her purse on the bar. Mags: 'Run it to her hotel? I can't leave the well.'

options.label: Run it across the bridge
options.get: A star who owes you one
options.cost: 15 Energy and a late Hailr home

outcomes.text: The concierge tries to stop you. Chardonnay herself comes down in a robe, hugs you and calls you 'the only honest person in Queens.'

later.text: Remember returning Chardonnay Shade's purse? She told the story on a podcast. You were 'an angel from Astoria.' Your follower count noticed.

options.label: Post what's inside first
options.get: 90 clout from a viral purse dump
options.riskWhy: Stars have lawyers on speed dial

outcomes.text: Three lipsticks, a parking ticket and a handwritten list titled 'Enemies (ranked).' The post is everywhere in an hour.

later.text: Remember posting Chardonnay's purse? Her lawyer called Mags. Mags called you. The Velvet Static door has your face on a sticky note.
later.headline: Developing: {name} posted Chardonnay Shade's purse before returning it. The 'Enemies (ranked)' list has a new name. 👀

title: Pigeons with ambition took Gus's bench. 'Thirty years that's my spot. Help me take it back.'

options.label: Sit with him till they leave
options.get: The bench back, and a story about 1987
options.cost: 8 Energy and an hour on cold wood

outcomes.text: You sit. Gus tells you about 1987. The pigeons, bored by 1987, leave. Gus says that's why he tells it.

options.label: Film him chasing them, post it
options.riskWhy: The whole park watches the internet

outcomes.text: Gus waving his cap at forty pigeons, slow motion, opera music. Two million views by dinner.

later.text: Remember the video of Gus vs. the pigeons? He saw it at the barbershop. He's not mad, he says. The whole park is mad for him.

options.label: Not today
options.riskWhy: Nobody keeps score of a no

outcomes.text: You tell Gus the pigeons have rights too. He looks at you like you're one of them.

title: Gus's hands shake too much to finish his grandson's wedding suit. 'Thread the needle for me?'

options.label: Sew with him all afternoon
options.get: A finished suit and an old tailor's thanks

outcomes.text: He talks, you thread, he sews. By sunset the suit is done and Gus holds it up to the river like a flag.

later.text: Remember threading Gus's needle? He made you a pocket square from the leftover wool. Everyone at the deli asks where you got it.

options.label: Help, at C$30 an hour
options.cost: Gus's pension, and his good opinion

outcomes.text: Four hours, C$120, a suit. Gus pays in exact change from a coin purse older than you, and doesn't tell any stories.

later.text: Remember charging Gus by the hour? His grandson gave a toast about 'a helper with a meter running.' The whole wedding knew who he meant.

options.label: Not today
options.riskWhy: Nobody keeps score of a no

outcomes.text: You tell Gus your hands shake too. He laughs and says 'then we're two old men.'

title: Gus bet his rival C$200 and his eyes are bad today. 'Be my eyes. Just call the dice, honest.'

options.label: Call the dice honestly
options.get: A seat at the bench, for life
options.cost: An hour of shouting about doubles

outcomes.text: Double sixes, called true. Gus wins and splits it: 'C$50 for the eyes.' His rival demands a rematch and a new set of eyes.
You call every roll true and Gus still loses. He laughs, pays up and tells you this is how it went in 1987 too.

options.label: Call them wrong for the rival

outcomes.text: A four becomes a two, twice. Gus loses by a hair. His rival tucks C$150 in your jacket during the handshake.

later.text: Remember misreading the dice for Gus? His rival bragged about the C$150 at the bench. Gus moved benches. Gus has never moved benches.
later.headline: BREAKING: Astoria Park in shock after {name} threw a backgammon game against Gus. Gus has moved benches. Sources say the pigeons took the old one.

title: Andreas has a name-day party for forty and his waiter is stuck on a dead N train. 'Opa? Please?'

options.label: Wait tables all night
options.cost: 22 Energy and forty orders of octopus

outcomes.text: Forty plates out, forty back empty, one 'Opa!' you'll hear in your sleep. Andreas kisses you on both cheeks and both hands.

later.text: Remember the name-day rush at Feta Compli? Andreas sent C$150 and a tray of spanakopita with your name written in phyllo.

options.label: Name your price, then triple it
options.cost: Andreas's night, at his worst moment
options.riskWhy: 30th Avenue talks at every name day

outcomes.text: Andreas pays C$300 before you tie the apron, sighing like his grandmother. You do a fine job. That's not the part he remembers.

later.text: Remember your triple rate at Feta Compli? Andreas told 30th Avenue. Every name day on the block somehow forgot your invitation.

options.label: Not today
options.riskWhy: Nobody keeps score of a no

outcomes.text: You tell Andreas you're busy. He says 'nobody is busy on a name day' and calls his cousin, sadly.

title: A food critic comes to Feta Compli tonight. Andreas: 'Taste the octopus. Be honest. Be kind. Mostly kind.'

options.label: Tell him the truth: more lemon
options.get: A better octopus and a grateful host
options.cost: The look on his face, briefly

outcomes.text: 'More lemon.' Andreas stares, then laughs so hard the bread basket falls. He adds lemon. He adds lemon to everything.

later.text: Remember telling Andreas 'more lemon'? The critic called it 'the best octopus in Queens.' Andreas tells everyone it was his idea, then winks at you.

outcomes.text: His cousin pays C$250 to know the critic's table time. The cousin's place gets a surprise visit first, and a surprise review.

later.text: Remember tipping off Andreas's cousin? It came out at a christening, in front of everyone. Andreas's door is shut to you for a while.
later.headline: Developing: {name} sold a food critic's reservation to the rival taverna. Andreas, on the record: 'Opa. But sad.'

title: Andreas is out of lemons. 'A taverna without lemons is a diner. Run to Steinway Fresh?'

options.label: Run for lemons
options.cost: 8 Energy and C$20 for the lemons
options.riskWhy: Steinway Fresh is busy at dinner

outcomes.text: Two bags of lemons, one sprint down Steinway. Andreas squeezes one over your head like a blessing. It's a blessing.

later.text: Remember the lemon run? Andreas named a dessert after you. It's mostly lemon. It's very good.

options.label: Charge C$120 for C$20 of lemons
options.riskWhy: The receipt is in the bag

outcomes.text: 'Lemons are expensive right now,' you say. They are not. Andreas pays C$120 because the dining room is full and he has no choice.

later.text: Remember the C$120 lemons? Andreas found the C$20 receipt in the bag. He taped it by the register, under 'Do not give lemons to.'

title: Arben's oven door broke mid-rush. 'Hold it shut. Gently. Like it's family.'

options.label: Hold the oven door for an hour
options.get: Free slices and Arben's slow smile

outcomes.text: An hour of holding a door at 500 degrees. The rush gets fed. Arben folds you a slice and says 'like a local.'

options.label: Film the meltdown for your feed
options.riskWhy: Comment sections are mean about crust

outcomes.text: Smoke, shouting, a slice on the floor. It's beautiful content. Arben is too busy to notice your phone.

later.text: Remember filming Arben's oven meltdown? The comments were cruel about his crust. His daughter read them. Arben read them to you.

options.label: Not today
options.riskWhy: Nobody keeps score of a no

outcomes.text: You back away from the heat. Arben holds the door shut with a mop and his whole personality.

title: Arben's daughter has her soccer final at four. 'Watch the counter? A dollar a slice. Spiritually.'

options.label: Watch the counter
options.get: Arben at the game, and a debt of pizza
options.cost: 18 Energy and a few burnt fingers

outcomes.text: You fold slices, take cash and shout at a man with a fork. Arben comes back glowing: she scored. Twice.

later.text: Remember watching Arben's counter? His daughter brought you the game ball. Arben brought a whole pie with your name in pepperoni.

options.label: Charge two dollars, keep one
options.riskWhy: Regulars know the price by heart

outcomes.text: Two dollars a slice all afternoon. A hundred-something slices later, there's C$200 in your pocket and the register looks exactly right.

later.text: Remember the two-dollar slices? Three regulars told Arben before he took his coat off. You paid back every dollar, plus a lecture.
later.headline: BREAKING: {name} ran Still-a-Dollar Slice for one afternoon and doubled the price. Arben: 'The sign is sentimental. You are not.'

options.label: Not today
options.riskWhy: Nobody keeps score of a no

outcomes.text: You can't today. Arben closes for two hours and the whole block acts like it's a holiday.

title: A candidate wants to film an ad at Arben's. 'He'll eat with a fork. Help me say no politely?'

options.label: Do the talking for him
options.cost: 6 Energy and one awkward campaign aide

outcomes.text: You tell the aide the lighting is bad and the slices are 'not camera trained.' They leave. Arben gives you a slow, proud nod.

options.label: Take a 'location fee,' let them film
options.cost: Arben's peace, and a fork on camera

outcomes.text: The campaign pays you C$300 as 'local consultant.' The candidate eats a slice with a fork and a knife. Arben has to sit down.

later.text: Remember the fork ad? It aired. Still-a-Dollar Slice is right there, fork in the foreground. Arben taped your photo inside the register. Not fondly.
later.headline: Developing: Campaign ad shot at Still-a-Dollar Slice features a fork. Sources say {name} took the location fee. Arben is 'still recovering.'

title: Tournament Friday and Pixel's ref bailed. 'Ref it? You just say no a lot. Like a parent.'

options.label: Ref the tournament straight
options.cost: 15 Energy and a lot of booing

outcomes.text: Six hours, nine finals, one tantrum from a grown man in a headset. Every call fair. Pixel names you 'Ref of the Year,' a title invented on the spot.

later.text: Remember refereeing Respawn Arena's Friday? The Arcade Nerds saved you a good chair. That has never happened to anyone.

options.label: Take a team's C$250
options.get: C$250 for a few close calls
options.riskWhy: Everything at an arcade is streamed

outcomes.text: A team captain slips you C$250 by the claw machine. You make three very generous calls. They win. Pixel hands them the trophy, frowning.

later.text: Remember the close calls at Tournament Friday? The losing team's stream clipped every one. Pixel banned you from the cabinets and made you refund the prize.
later.headline: BREAKING: Respawn Arena's Tournament Friday was rigged, sources say, by {name} with a whistle. Pixel: 'The honor system is failing.'

title: The energy-drink honor fridge is C$300 short. Pixel: 'Watch it with me tonight? I need to know.'

options.label: Stake out the fridge
options.cost: 15 Energy and a night under neon

outcomes.text: Midnight. A hooded figure. It's Chase Clout, filming himself 'stealing for the content.' Pixel bans him for the third time. You get the good chair.
Nobody comes. Pixel buys a padlock. You both eat chips at 2 AM and talk about cabinet three's high score.

options.label: Watch it, and help yourself
options.get: Free drinks and C$80 from the box
options.cost: The fridge, and Pixel's faith in it

outcomes.text: You 'keep watch' with three cans and the honor box in reach. By morning you're wired, C$80 richer, and the fridge is more short.

later.text: Remember the stakeout at Respawn Arena? Pixel forgot there was a camera. Then he remembered. You're on the wall of shame, next to Chase Clout.

options.label: Not today
options.riskWhy: Nobody keeps score of a no

outcomes.text: You tell Pixel you've got an early day. He nods and tapes a sad face to the fridge door.

title: Skyler Beta's app wants to sponsor the arena. Pixel: 'Test it? If it crashes, I need a reason to say no.'

options.label: Test it honestly
options.get: Pixel's arena, saved from a bad deal
options.riskWhy: Testing apps is its own punishment

outcomes.text: It crashes on launch, at login and once while closing. You write it all up. Pixel says no with a three-page report and a smile.

options.label: Tell Pixel it's great, for a cut
options.cost: Pixel's tournament, on a broken app

outcomes.text: Skyler pays you C$300 to say the app is 'seamless.' You say it. Pixel signs. Skyler sends a heart emoji and a contract.

later.text: Remember vouching for Skyler Beta's app? It crashed during Tournament Friday, live, on the big screen. Pixel told everyone who said 'seamless.'
later.headline: Developing: Skyler Beta's app crashed live at Respawn Arena. Sources say {name} called it 'seamless.' We reached out. The app crashed.

title: Lola's best source went quiet. 'Babe, sit in the booth at Neon Spoon and listen. Just listen.'

options.label: Listen, report only facts
options.get: A friend in the gossip business
options.cost: 10 Energy and an evening of overhearing
options.riskWhy: Most of it is about parking

outcomes.text: Two hours of eavesdropping. Mostly parking, one real engagement. You bring Lola only what you heard. She calls it 'clean tea' and buys your dessert.

later.text: Remember sitting in Lola's booth? Your tip checked out. She called you 'a source with receipts' in her column. Everybody read it.

options.label: Spice it up, make some up
options.cost: Lola's column, and whoever you named

outcomes.text: Nothing happened, so you make something happen: a secret wedding, a fake breakup. Lola posts it. The comments explode. You're 'a source close to it.'

later.text: Remember the tea you gave Lola? None of it was true. She ran a correction with your initials. Lola has never run a correction before.
later.headline: CORRECTION: Lola Lowdown regrets the secret wedding story. Sources say it came from {name}. On the record: 'Never again, sweetie.'

title: Lola's phone died on deadline. 'Lend me yours? Five minutes. I won't read your texts. Much.'

options.label: Hand it over
options.cost: Five minutes of her in your camera roll

outcomes.text: She posts the story, reads three of your texts and gives the phone back warm. 'Your ex is still typing, babe. Don't.'

later.text: Remember lending Lola your phone? She mentioned you in her column: 'a real one, with a full battery.' People asked for your number.

options.label: Rent it to her by the minute

outcomes.text: 'C$20 a minute.' Lola pays without blinking, posts the story, and writes something in a tiny notebook. It's your name.

later.text: Remember renting Lola your phone? She wrote you into the column as 'a source who invoices.' Doors got a little colder.

options.label: Not today
options.riskWhy: Nobody keeps score of a no

outcomes.text: Your battery is at 4% too. Lola says 'tragic,' and borrows the waiter's.

title: Tourists in matching shirts took Lola's table. 'Sweetie, I need it back before the nine o'clock spill.'

options.label: Talk them to the next table
options.get: Lola's table back, and her seal of approval
options.cost: 8 Energy and too many group photos

outcomes.text: You tell them the next table 'gets the better light for photos.' They move. Lola sits, spills at nine sharp, and points at you: 'Mine.'

options.label: Sell them 'the famous seat'
options.cost: Lola's table, on her big night

outcomes.text: 'That's Lola Lowdown's table, the most famous seat in Queens.' They pay C$200 to keep it all night. Lola spills standing up.

later.text: Remember selling Lola's table? She posted the receipt. She always has the receipt. The Neon Spoon host has your face on a list.
later.headline: BREAKING: {name} sold Lola Lowdown's table to a tour group. Allegedly. With receipts.

title: Sgt. Bev has a parking report in triplicate and the copier died. 'Got neat handwriting, hon?'

options.label: Copy it out by hand, three times
options.get: Bev's favor, which is a real thing
options.cost: 12 Energy and a cramp in your hand

outcomes.text: Three copies of a fight about a parking spot, word for word. Bev reads one and says 'beautiful,' which she has never said about paperwork.

later.text: Remember the triplicate at the 114½? Bev 'misfiled' a parking ticket of yours. C$65, gone. Lola says that's love.

options.label: Lose your own ticket in the pile

outcomes.text: While you copy, your own parking ticket slides into the shredder. Very neat handwriting. Very neat crime.

later.text: Remember 'helping' with Bev's paperwork? The fourth copy turned up. Bev gave you two hours on the bench to think about carbon paper.
later.headline: Developing: {name} spent two hours at the 114½ Precinct over a parking ticket that 'fell into a shredder.' Sgt. Bev: 'I write it down. That's the service.'

title: It's Pierogi Friday and Sgt. Bev's order never came. 'I can't leave. I'm the whole desk.'

options.label: Pick up her pierogi
options.get: Bev's best mood of the week
options.cost: 10 Energy and C$25 for the order
options.riskWhy: The pierogi place has a line

outcomes.text: A dozen pierogi, still warm. Bev eats one, closes her eyes and says 'quiet night' like a prayer. It works for an hour.

later.text: Remember Bev's pierogi run? She told Lola you're 'good people.' Lola posted it. Being vouched for by a cop and a gossip at once is a lot.

options.label: Eat a few on the way
options.get: A full stomach and some Energy
options.cost: Bev's dozen, now eleven. Then nine.

outcomes.text: One on the subway stairs. Two at the corner. You hand Bev the bag. 'Nine is not a dozen, hon.'

later.text: Remember Bev's short dozen? She did the math. You did an hour on the precinct bench. Bev did a word search.

options.label: Not today
options.riskWhy: Nobody keeps score of a no

outcomes.text: You tell Bev you're not a delivery app. She writes it down. That's the service.

title: A car alarm has wailed outside the 114½ for an hour. Bev: 'Find whose it is. I'll owe you one.'

options.label: Knock on every door on the block
options.get: A quiet street and a sergeant's favor
options.cost: 15 Energy and a lot of 'not mine'

outcomes.text: Fourteen doors. The fifteenth: a man asleep in headphones. He turns it off. The block applauds from its windows. Bev raises her mug.

later.text: Remember the car alarm outside the 114½? Bev 'owes you one,' she says, and buys you a coffee in her World's Okayest Cop mug. It's an honor.

options.label: Find the owner, charge a fee
options.get: C$150 to keep it off the tow list
options.cost: Bev's name, used to shake someone down

outcomes.text: You find him, tell him the tow is coming 'unless,' and take C$150 to 'talk to the sergeant.' You never talk to the sergeant.

later.text: Remember charging the car alarm guy to 'talk to the sergeant'? He came in to thank Bev. Bev gave you an hour on the bench and his C$150 back.
later.headline: BREAKING: {name} charged a neighbor C$150 to 'talk to the sergeant.' The sergeant, on the record: 'Nobody talks to me. Get on line.'

title: Someone actually wants to buy a suitcase. Pablo: 'Talk them out of it. I don't know the prices.'

options.label: Point them to a real luggage shop
options.riskWhy: Customers don't like being turned away

outcomes.text: You walk the customer to a real luggage store on Steinway. Pablo watches from the door and gives you a mint, which is the highest honor.

options.label: Sell the load-bearing one for C$450
options.get: C$450 for a very old suitcase

outcomes.text: C$450, cash, for the brown one at the bottom of the stack. The customer leaves happy. The shelf above makes a small sound.

later.text: Remember selling Pablo's load-bearing suitcase? The back wall shifted an inch. Pablo sent you a bill, a mint and a look. Pay the bill.

options.label: Not today
options.riskWhy: Nobody keeps score of a no

outcomes.text: You tell Pablo you don't do retail. He nods. 'Nobody does. That's the business model.'

title: Pablo's notary license has been 'pending since 2009.' 'Help me fill in the renewal? I don't read forms.'

options.label: Fill it in, truthfully
options.get: A legal notary on Steinway, finally
options.cost: 12 Energy and a form in triplicate

outcomes.text: Nineteen pages. You read every one. Pablo winces at the word 'address.' It goes in the mail, an honest envelope for once.

later.text: Remember Pablo's renewal? It came through after seventeen years. He framed it, then hid the frame. He pressed C$200 into your hand. 'Don't count it here.'

options.label: Rent out his stamp while you're at it
options.riskWhy: Sgt. Bev likes to look at everything

outcomes.text: While the form waits, you stamp twelve strangers' papers at C$30 each, no questions. Pablo would be proud, if he knew. He doesn't.

later.text: Remember stamping papers with Pablo's seal? One was a lease for a closet inside a closet. Sgt. Bev came by, bought nothing and took you for a chat.
later.headline: Developing: {name} notarized a lease for a closet inside a closet with a borrowed stamp. Sgt. Bev: 'I write it down. That's the service.'

title: Auntie Bee has a cold and won't ask for help. Pablo: 'Bring her soup? She'd never let me.'

options.label: Bring soup and sit with her
options.cost: 12 Energy and C$20 for the soup

outcomes.text: Auntie Bee says she's fine, eats two bowls, beats you at cards and tells you about Pablo in 2009. You will never unhear it.

later.text: Remember the soup for Auntie Bee? She knitted you a scarf with a pocket nobody would think to check. Pablo's people nod at you on the street now.

options.label: Cover her counter, keep her cut
options.cost: Auntie Bee's money, while she's sick

outcomes.text: You cover her shift at the counter and keep the envelope Pablo leaves for her. C$300. Auntie Bee is too sick to ask. For now.

later.text: Remember Auntie Bee's envelope? She's better now, and she asked. Pablo made you pay it back. His door is 'closed.' It's always closed, but now it means it.

options.label: Not today
options.riskWhy: Nobody keeps score of a no

outcomes.text: You tell Pablo you don't do sickbeds. He sends Tito, who brings a fan instead of soup.
